result.markdown: --- title: "04 · Categorical predictors" subtitle: "Week 1" --- ::: {.guiding-q} What if a predictor is a category? ::: ## In this session - Dummy (treatment) coding and the reference level - What the coefficients of a factor mean - Other contrasts (sum coding) and when to use them - Estimated marginal means and pairwise comparisons with `emmeans` ::: {.key-terms} **Key terms:** [Contrasts and dummy coding](../../glossary.qmd#contrasts), [Reference level](../../glossary.qmd#reference-level), [Estimated marginal means](../../glossary.qmd#emmeans) ::: ## Learning goals After this session you can - explain how R turns a factor into numeric predictors, - interpret coefficients relative to a reference level, - obtain group means and contrasts with `emmeans`. ## Simulate first ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(4) group <- factor(rep(c("control", "food", "toy"), each = 20)) mu <- c(control = 10, food = 14, toy = 12) y <- rnorm(60, mu[group], 3) m <- lm(y ~ group) round(coef(m), 2) # intercept = control, others = differences ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` #> (Intercept) groupfood grouptoy #> 11.13 3.79 0.85 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} head(model.matrix(m)[c(1, 21, 41), ]) # the dummy variables behind the scenes ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` #> (Intercept) groupfood grouptoy #> 1 1 0 0 #> 21 1 1 0 #> 41 1 0 1 ``` ::: ::: ## Materials ::: {.materials} - Slides coming soon - R script coming soon - Exercises coming soon ::: ## Reading - Schad, D. J., Vasishth, S., Hohenstein, S., & Kliegl, R. (2020). How to capitalize on a priori contrasts in linear (mixed) models: A tutorial. *Journal of Memory and Language, 110*, 104038.
